question: Which of the following is India’s oldest city?
solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Varanasi.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Varanasi **is possibly** India's oldest continually inhabited city** and has been a cradle of** Indian Vedic culture.**
 
• Varanasi has been bustling with cultural and devout activity since the **Bronze Age collapse.**
 
• Varanasi is one of the **world's oldest continually settled cities. **
 
• Kashi, its old name, was related to a **kingdom of the same name of 2,500 years ago. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anangpal Tomar** established **Delhi in 1052.**
 
• The registered history of **Aligarh **starts with the establishment of the **Aligarh Fort in the 16th century.**
 
• Vibrant and global **Lucknow** earned fame as the seat of the **Nawabs of Awadh in the 18th century.​**
 
• **Asaf -Ud-Daula, son of Shuja-ud- Daula**, transferred the capital from **Faizabad to Lucknow in 1775** and made it one of the most wealthy and shining **cities in all India. **
